result.title: RW-Flow: One-Step Generation on Compact Manifolds via Wasserstein Gradient Flows
result.summary: Manifold-valued data, and consequently the distributions they induce, are prevalent across many domains, ranging from the locations of geospatial events, such as earthquakes, to biomolecular torsion angles that encode information about three-dimensional structure. While diffusion and flow-based generative models have been successfully extended to compact manifolds, sampling typically requires tens or hundreds of sequential network evaluations. We introduce RW-Flow, a theoretically grounded framework for learning one-step generative models on compact manifolds via Wasserstein gradient flows. The main challenge is identifiability: driving the velocity field to zero should guarantee that the model distribution matches the target distribution. We establish a necessary and sufficient condition for identifiability on compact, connected Riemannian manifolds. We specifically show that, for a symmetric, Lipschitz-continuous cost function, the velocity field induced by the Sinkhorn divergence is identifiable if and only if the associated Gibbs kernel is nondegenerate. This characterization provides a general principle for designing identifiable costs on compact manifolds. It also reveals that the squared geodesic distance, the natural manifold analogue of the squared Euclidean distance, does not always guarantee identifiability. Across benchmarks involving geospatial events, protein side chain torsion angles, RNA backbone torsion angles, and general manifolds discretized as triangular meshes, RW-Flow outperforms existing one-step methods in nearly all settings under fair comparison conditions.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 RW-Flow，利用 Wasserstein 梯度流在紧致黎曼流形上学习一步生成模型，并给出速度场可辨识性的充要条件（与 Sinkhorn 散度对应的 Gibbs 核非退化相关），在地震位置、蛋白质侧链与 RNA 骨架扭转角及三角网格基准上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心概念——通过使速度场归零来保证模型分布匹配目标分布的可辨识性刻画——可能与 LVR 中 latent 状态是否真正被答案使用、以及轨迹训练中的贡献分配与停止判据有概念联系，可作为「状态收敛即证据充分」这类表述的核查线索；但该工作是纯生成建模、无视觉或多模态推理，迁移性尚需人工判断。
